decision.summary: The Fed held its policy rate at 5% to 5.25%. The vote was 11-0.

changes.quote: Recent indicators suggest that economic activity has continued to expand at a modest pace.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Economic activity expanded at a modest pace in the first quarter.”

changes.quote: In support of these goals, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 5 to 5-1/4 percent.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “In support of these goals, the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 5 to 5-1/4 percent.”

changes.quote: Holding the target range steady at this meeting allows the Committee to assess additional information and its implications for monetary policy.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “The Committee will closely monitor incoming information and assess the implications for monetary policy.”

changes.quote: In determining the extent of additional policy firming that may be appropriate to return inflation to 2 percent over time, the Committee will take into account the cumulative tightening of monetary policy, the lags with which monetary policy affects economic activity and inflation, and economic and financial developments.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “In determining the extent to which additional policy firming may be appropriate to return inflation to 2 percent over time, the Committee will take into account…”

tone_quotes.quote: In determining the extent of additional policy firming that may be appropriate to return inflation to 2 percent over time, the Committee will take into account the cumulative tightening of monetary policy, the lags with which monetary policy affects economic activity and inflation, and economic and financial developments.
The Committee is strongly committed to returning inflation to its 2 percent objective.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 20.09% APR costs about $83.71 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 3.83% and moved -1 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 6.79% would fall by about $2.00 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 3.6%, and employers added an average of 196k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 4.1% over the past year (May 2023); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 4.8%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 3.4% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +7 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved 0.08%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.35% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is hawkish (leaning toward higher rates). The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 24%, cut 1%, hike 76%.
